facts.text: QuadrotorPlusHoverEnv-v0 is registered with frame_skip=5, env_bounding_box=1.2 and randomize_reset=True
The QuadrotorPlusHoverEnv constructor defaults are xml_name quadrotor_plus.xml, frame_skip 5, env_bounding_box 1.2 and randomize_reset False
The policy action range is -1.0 to 1.0 and the safe policy range is -0.8 to 0.8
step clips the action to the policy range and maps it to motor inputs hover_force + action * 2.0 / (policy_range[1] - policy_range[0])
step updates the time counter and clips the action to the policy range before the motor input is computed
The observation is an 18-value vector: the position error (3), the flattened 3x3 rotation matrix, linear velocity (3) and angular velocity (3), concatenated in that order

The reward sums a position term (position error norm times -position_reward_constant), an orientation term, linear and angular velocity terms, an action term, the alive bonus, the goal bonus, the bound penalty and a velocity-towards-goal term, all times reward_scaling_coefficient

The reward constants default to bonus_to_reach_goal 15.0, max_reward_for_velocity_towards_goal 2.0, position 5.0, orientation 0.02, linear velocity 0.01, angular velocity 0.001, action 0.0025, reward_for_staying_alive 5.0 and reward_scaling_coefficient 1.0
done is True when the observation is not finite, the position error norm is not below env_bounding_box_norm, or _time is not below max_time_steps
env_bounding_box defaults to 1.2 and is the per-axis initial position error bound

With randomize=False the reset starts at the desired position with zero velocity; with randomize=True it draws a position offset within env_bounding_box - 0.2 of the desired position and velocities within init_max_vel and init_max_angular_vel
The model timestep is 0.01 s and gravity is -9.81 in z
The four motors are ctrl-limited to the range 0 to 1
The README names QuadrotorPlusHoverEnv-v0, TiltrotorPlus8DofHoverEnv-v0 and QuadrotorXHoverEnv-v0 as the available environments

determinism.notes: reset(seed) fixes the initial state and the fake's dynamics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the fake draws initial states with Python's random.Random and upstream with numpy's generator, so a seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: the fake is a damped toy model, not a MuJoCo integration of the quadrotor: it does not model contacts, thrust vectoring, rotor dynamics or the rigid-body equations, and it keeps the rotation matrix at the identity

the fake's action space is a four-element Box 0 to 1 taken from the model's actuator ctrlrange; the action space inherited from gym's MuJoCo base class is outside the clone, was not available where the gate ran and was not compared with the fake's
initial states use Python's random.Random while the upstream environment uses numpy's generator, so a seed does not give the same trajectory on the two
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by 50 ms (0.01 s model timestep times the registered frame_skip 5) only
no rendering, no viewer and no mujoco_py: the fake returns plain Python floats where upstream returns numpy arrays
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
